claims.summary: Authenticated multipart transcription executes an active CPU recipe on WAV or FLAC through native workflow and session owners, returning JSON text with bounded admission, cancellation and run lineage. Small-encoder integration evidence only; streaming, timestamps and full-model quality are not claimed.
Safetensors repositories apply config, index, shard, header, tensor, dtype, range, overlap, and catalog bounds.
Standard Llama and Qwen2 Safetensors metadata, names, shapes, storage, and payload streams bridge to existing GGUF runtime catalogs.
Qwen 3.5 Safetensors text, recurrent, and MTP metadata, names, shapes, and payload streams bridge to existing GGUF runtime catalogs.
GGUF parsing applies allocation, count, alignment, and split limits.
Qwen3.5-4B recurrent layer 0 trains from the real GGUF and real prompt token embeddings through the compiled resident program; adaptive_new has no corresponding training oracle.

Gemma E4B layer 0 trains its real per-layer adapter on fingerprinted text, image, and audio representations through a compiled device-Muon program with exact checkpoint resume; complete 42-layer training remains open.

OvergoDB objective documents approve text-to-text, image-to-text, and audio-to-text only after real corpus processing, E4B tokenizer/projector execution, adapter gradients, device Muon, and token evaluation; the other 33 single-modality pairs are refused.

OvergoDB objective kind and modality facts bind adaptive FNS, latent L2, latent-sequence L2, forecast, OCR token, flow-matching, image-latent, and logit-distillation contracts to the shared forward/backward/Muon program; a missing program is refused.
Multimodal requests bound encoded bodies, decoded media, dimensions, and pixels.
Gemma4 12B image and audio prompts reach language on CUDA with pinned first-token evidence; real video retains frame order and block masks through language.
Gemma E4B waveform frontend and audio tower match fingerprinted adaptive log-mel, 12-layer conformer, and soft-token evidence on CUDA.
Gemma E4B image projection binds the exact adaptive prompt and produces the fingerprinted first language token on CUDA.
Qwen3.5 image and 16-frame video inputs match pinned Python processor, projector, prompt, MRoPE, and first-language-token oracles on CUDA.
RxBrain real-image VQA executes through a compiled and verified recipe, reproduces the exact golden token prefix and coherent EOS answer, then replays bit-exactly through the active alias.
Audio attention policy is a canonical content-addressed profile bound separately from language architecture policy.
Split GGUF models load, validate, write, merge, and round-trip.
Quantization encoders are checked against pinned GGML references.
CUDA driver work executes through one locked-thread context owner.
Model opening compiles per-layer graph, cache, attention, position, residual, and feed-forward policy before execution.
Repeated CUDA graph execution can reuse validated topology, BLAS selection, and arena planning.
Tensor operation identity, diagnostic class, and backend coverage share one typed catalog.
Bounded prompt caches support selection, eviction, context edits, and exact media-signed replay.
GBNF and JSON Schema constraints match pinned upstream corpora.
Native, Chat, and Responses prompts preserve ordered image/text parts.
Chat and Responses preserve projected images in earlier or final user turns through the complete formatted history.
Gemma 4 preserves ordered image/audio chunks through native, Chat, and Responses history.
Remote media is opt-in through explicit scheme, host, port, network, redirect, timeout, MIME, concurrency, and byte policy.
Responses accepts bounded typed inline, policy-mapped file-ID, allowlisted URL, and image file-ID inputs.
Chat, Responses, and Anthropic tool histories use one recipe-admitted typed executor; unsupported tool types are refused.
Chat and Responses decode bounded single-turn encoded video through native GIF or FFmpeg paths.
Chat and Responses token counts use the projected media prompt.
Native generation and the Chat, Responses, and Anthropic protocols share prepared prompts with token counting.
Chat, Responses, and Anthropic stream JSON and Hermes function arguments incrementally.
Chat, Responses, and Anthropic preserve projected image/audio history while formatting and streaming function tools.
Anthropic image blocks support bounded base64, allowlisted URL, and mapped file-ID projection with token-count parity.
Manual summarized thinking supports buffered/SSE output, projected images, handler-local signed replay, and tamper rejection.
OvergoDB-backed interaction records preserve text, media, tool-call, streaming, and token-count continuations across server restarts.
Responses reasoning summaries support input replay, buffered output, streaming lifecycle events, and continuation retention.
Model architectures use a central family and capability registry with grouped specifications.
Graph construction and tensor catalog validation route through compiled neutral layer programs, superseding the removed compatibility-layer family dispatcher.
Retained CUDA cache pages and transactional attention/recurrent/hybrid multi-sequence steps support dynamic admission and forks.
Rectangular encoder-decoder batches use explicit source and decoder lengths so padding never enters attention state.
Release archives are deterministic and compared across two builds.
Pocket-TTS executes through its compiled speech recipe and matches pinned latent, EOS, PCM, WAV, rate, channel, and heap evidence.
The embedded workbench replays bounded plain-causal attention on host and refuses compiled score policies it cannot reproduce exactly.
The authenticated GUI reads the active OvergoDB dataset catalog without dataset mutation or payload access.
The authenticated GUI pages bounded read-only OvergoDB run records through the canonical run decoder.
SenseNova text requests execute through compiled routed-image recipe modules, retained CUDA generation, and fingerprinted PNG publication.
